text:
Fixed candidates enable paired comparisons but define a sampled-ranking benchmark: HR@10 against 99 negatives need not preserve full-catalog model rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Keep users, candidates, preprocessing and seeds identical across variants. For this setup, report four category HRs and their equally weighted mean. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Applying [paired-bootstrap principles](https://people.csail.mit.edu/koehn/publications/bootstrap2004.pdf), resample 200 users with replacement independently within each category, keeping each user’s outcomes paired across models; compute the macro difference per replicate and report its 95% interval. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the four datasets, fixed candidates and trained checkpoints—not candidate-sampling or training randomness.

Repeatedly selecting architectures, hyperparameters and checkpoints on the same validation sample creates adaptive overfitting; ordinary bootstrap intervals around the selected winner do not correct that selection bias ([Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)). Practical safeguards: prespecify evaluation cadence, checkpoint rule, search limits and tie-breaking; log every attempted variant and validation look; treat post-selection intervals as descriptive. Preserve the pinned splits and evaluator, freeze the complete selection before the host’s independent held-out evaluation, and make no test-driven revisions.

Compare methods at matched cumulative GPU-seconds, counting tuning, diagnostics and failed runs—not merely equal epochs or successful trials. Report best validation performance versus consumed compute, checkpoint counts and training exposure; retain seed 42 for the required comparison. Additional seed experiments, if permitted and affordable, must be budgeted and reported separately. Search-budget reporting matters because model rankings can change with tuning resources ([Dodge et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.03004)).
